- document:
  - link "Skip to main content":

  - main:

    - text: March 12, 2017
    - heading "Engineering Safety with Uber’s Real-Time ID Check" [level=1]
    - img "Dima Kovalev"
    - text: Dima Kovalev
    - img "Nitin Bajaj"
    - text: Nitin Bajaj
    - img "Shimul Sachdeva"
    - text: Shimul Sachdeva
    - img "Header Image for Engineering Safety"
    - text: Share this article
    - button "Facebook":
      - img "Facebook"
    - button "Linkedin":
      - img "Linkedin"
    - button "X social":
      - img "X social"
    - button "Link":
      - img "Link"
    - paragraph:
      - text: Safety and security are at the core of Uber’s business. An important part of safety is verifying that the driver-partner who is picking up riders is the same person who underwent Uber’s screening process. Through engineering, we have taken a proactive approach through a new security solution called
      - link "Real-Time ID Check":
        - /url: https://newsroom.uber.com/securityselfies/
      - text: which ensures the right person is behind the wheel.
    - figure "Real-Time ID Check ensures that the driver-partner picking you up is the same person who underwent Uber’s screening process."
    - paragraph: This feature protects riders from unverified drivers, and also prevents fraud by ensuring drivers’ accounts are not compromised. Here is the story of how the safety team in Uber Engineering recently built this critical tool.
    - heading "Building a Solution with Selfies" [level=3]:
      - strong: Building a Solution with Selfies
    - paragraph: To build an effective and scalable solution, we needed a technology that could be deployed around the globe and still provide results with a high level of confidence. We started by evaluating various cutting edge technical solutions in face, voice, and gesture recognition. Each technology introduced unique challenges, especially given the high degree of environmental variance where our product is used around the world.
    - paragraph: One challenge with voice recognition solutions was that their performance drastically degraded with background interference from music and traffic. This solution was also impractical for speech-impaired driver-partners on our platform. Gesture recognition algorithms delivered promising results in a controlled environment with a limited set of tech-savvy users. However, it did not meet our global scale requirements due to user experience challenges and a steep learning curve.
    - paragraph: "Face verification stood out on top compared to all other solutions we evaluated. A typical face verification algorithm involves three main steps:"
    - list:
      - listitem: "Face Detection: Identify a face in a given image. If a face is not detected, the next steps are skipped as there is no face to match."
      - listitem: "Feature Extraction: Build a feature set by extracting facial features, like eye position and face shape, from the image."
      - listitem: "Face Matching: Compare the feature set with an already validated feature set for a given face."
    - paragraph:
      - text: Once we decided to use face verification, we explored a few leading vendors and ran a comparison analysis. We plotted each vendor’s results as a ratio of the true positive rate (TPR) against the false positive rate (FPR) over varying degrees of match confidence thresholds. The resulting receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve allowed us to determine the maximum TPR possible while minimizing FPR. Looking for the solution with the highest TPR, we ultimately chose to use
      - link "Microsoft’s Face API":
        - /url: https://www.microsoft.com/cognitive-services/en-us/face-api
      - text: from its Cognitive Services suite.
    - figure "A face detection example through Microsoft’s Face API."
    - paragraph: "Microsoft’s Face API was not only the most accurate in our testing, but it also provided a strong set of critical features for our product. Our Real-Time ID Check utilizes two specific APIs:"
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - link "Face-Detect":
          - /url: https://dev.projectoxford.ai/docs/services/563879b61984550e40cbbe8d/operations/563879b61984550f30395236
        - text: ": Detects human faces in an image and provides additional attributes, such as whether or not the face has glasses. This API is even smart enough to differentiate between reading glasses and sunglasses. This helped us filter out images without a face and improved the match score for verification of the selfies."
      - listitem:
        - link "Face-Verify":
          - /url: https://dev.projectoxford.ai/docs/services/563879b61984550e40cbbe8d/operations/563879b61984550f3039523a
        - text: ": Compares a face detected from Face-Detect API with an already verified face, and provides a confidence score on whether the two faces belong to the same person or not. Based on the confidence score, we can take appropriate verification action, such as asking the user to retake the selfie."
    - heading "The User Experience" [level=3]:
      - strong: The User Experience
    - paragraph: One of the key objectives for Real-Time ID Check was to avoid unnecessary friction for driver- partners. Therefore, we focused on making the user experience as seamless as possible throughout every stage of the project. We refined designs and tweaked the engineering based on feedback from users and prototype testing. This enabled us to create a simple, yet effective experience that drivers can complete in only a few seconds.
    - paragraph
    - paragraph:
      - iframe
    - paragraph: "Here is what that experience looks like:"
    - list:
      - listitem: Driver-partners are selected at random to submit a selfie for verification.
      - listitem: Microsoft’s Face API is used to detect if the submitted picture contains a face or not. If no face is detected, the driver-partner is asked to resubmit.
      - listitem: Once a face is detected, Microsoft’s Face API Verify feature compares the face with the verified picture associated with the driver’s account.
      - listitem: If the face is a match, the driver-partner is allowed to start picking up riders. If the face does not match, the driver is temporarily blocked while we investigate the situation.
    - heading "From Prototype to Global Scale" [level=3]:
      - strong: From Prototype to Global Scale
    - paragraph: Early prototypes demonstrated that the global expectations of this identity-check tool—making it work for drivers anywhere—would bring its own set of unique challenges.
    - heading "Low-Light Conditions" [level=4]:
      - strong: Low-Light Conditions
    - paragraph: Our initial UI leveraged the existing photo capture experience of the Driver app for taking profile photos. We soon realized the dark background of the UI prevented usable results in low-light conditions such as night time. To address this challenge, we switched to a white UI and increased the brightness of the screen, leading to a drastic improvement in the quality of the photo captured.
    - figure "Black UI White UI In low light conditions, such as a parking lot at night, a light UI is crucial.":
      - link:
        - /url: https://www.uber.com/us/en/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/pjimage.jpg
      - emphasis
      - text: Black UI
      - emphasis
      - text: White UI In low light conditions, such as a parking lot at night, a light UI is crucial.
    - heading "Device Fragmentation" [level=4]:
      - strong: Device Fragmentation
    - paragraph: Before using Microsoft’s Face API, we originally used client-side face detection to ensure there was a face present in the selfie. However, low-end Android phones, used by many of our driver-partners, do not support face detection. Even some devices that claimed to support face detection did not function well.
    - paragraph: By using Microsoft’s Face API, we shifted the detection logic to the backend and removed these hardware constraints. This resulted in consistent results, regardless of the device, and gave us better insights to diagnose detection failures. Additionally, this process improved the quality of driver-partners’ profile photos.
    - heading "Selfie While Driving" [level=4]:
      - strong: Selfie While Driving
    - paragraph: To be an effective security measure, Real-Time ID Check asks randomly-selected driver-partners to verify their identity. Due to the random nature of this selection process, the request could potentially pop up while a driver-partner is driving. To prevent unsafe and distracted driving, we added movement detection using the driver’s phone GPS. If the vehicle is moving, we prompt drivers to pull over before they begin the verification flow.
    - figure "The feature uses a safety measure prompt if the vehicle is in motion."
    - heading "Selfies with Glasses" [level=3]:
      - strong: Selfies with Glasses
    - paragraph: "Although Microsoft’s Face API is able to detect a face even if the user is wearing sunglasses or if there is a reflection from regular glasses, these accessories can impact whether the new selfie will match the driver’s profile photo. In cases where the photos do not match and glasses are detected, the feature asks driver partners to remove their glasses and retry:"
    - figure "Glasses detection prevents bad verification scores.":
      - link:
        - /url: https://www.uber.com/us/en/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/figure-7-engineering-safety.png
      - text: Glasses detection prevents bad verification scores.
    - heading "Real World Impact" [level=3]:
      - strong: Real World Impact
    - paragraph: The true success of a product is reflected by the impact it makes in people’s lives. Since our initial launch in September 2016, well over 99% of driver-partners have been verified through Real-Time ID Check in the markets where it is available, and the majority of mismatches were due to unclear profile photos.
    - paragraph:
      - text: Riders can feel safe knowing that their driver has been verified and driver-partners can rest assured that a fraudster is not using their account. If you are interested in making a real world impact by engineering
      - link "safety and security":
        - /url: https://www.uber.com/us/en/safety/
      - text: with us,
      - link "come be a part of our story":
        - /url: https://www.uber.com/us/en/careers/list/?city=all&country=all&keywords=safety+telematics&subteam=all&team=engineering
      - text: .
    - figure "The proud Uber team behind Real-Time ID Check gets its own photo taken."
    - paragraph: Nitin Bajaj is a software engineer and Shimul Sachdeva is an engineering manager on Uber Engineering’s Trust & Safety program team. They wrote this article with Dima Kovalev, its product manager.
    - paragraph:
      - text: "This article is part of a continuing series on engineering safety: see"
      - link "our earlier article on Telematics":
        - /url: https://www.uber.com/us/en/blog/telematics/
      - text: for more on this type of work across Uber Engineering.
    - paragraph:
      - emphasis:
        - text: For more information on Uber’s Security & Privacy Teams in general, see their own
        - link "Uber Security + Privacy blog":
          - /url: https://medium.com/uber-security-privacy

  - text: DELIVERY TRACKING SOFTWARE
  - heading "Real-Time Visibility and Tracking Across Every Delivery" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Knowing a driver left the warehouse isn't the same as knowing when it'll be delivered. Onfleet provides real-time visibility into every order, even when the delivery is outsourced, so you always know where it is and when it will arrive.
  - link "Start free trial":

  - list:

      - img
      - heading "\"If you want to do deliveries in-house or through a third party, but still have visibility, Onfleet would be the solution for that.\"" [level=4]
      - paragraph: Robbin Constant, Delivery Manager & Last Mile Lead, Inspired Go
  - heading "The Delivery Platform That Sees Your Entire Operation, Not Just Your Fleet." [level=2]
  - paragraph: Onfleet gives you one place to track every delivery, understand every cost, and keep every customer informed, whether you’re delivering with your own drivers, third party providers, or both. No blind spots. No black boxes. No visibility gaps as your operation grows.
  - link "See how Onfleet does it":
    - /url: "#featuresTitle"
    - text: See how Onfleet does it
    - img
  - text: Onfleet by the Numbers 1B+
  - paragraph: Miles Tracked
  - text: 99%
  - paragraph: On-Time Deliveries
  - text: 80%
  - paragraph: Reduction in Customer Support Inquiries
  - text: 30+
  - paragraph: Webhooks to trigger Notifications
  - heading "Give Your Team Real-Time Visibility of Every Delivery, In-House or Outsourced" [level=2]
  - img "Unified Delivery Tracking"
  - img "Live Command Center"
  - img "Accurate, Predictive ETAs"
  - heading "Unified Delivery Tracking" [level=3]
  - paragraph: Track deliveries across your internal drivers and any third-party partners in the same view. Whether you run your own fleet, work with couriers, or both, every order stays visible from dispatch to delivery.
  - heading "Live Command Center" [level=3]
  - paragraph: A real-time map of every active route, with turn-by-turn progress, delay alerts, and the ability to reassign or intervene before a problem becomes a missed delivery. No more calling drivers to find out where they are.
  - heading "Accurate, Predictive ETAs" [level=3]
  - paragraph: AI-powered ETAs update dynamically for your drivers based on GPS location and historical traffic patterns, flagging at-risk deliveries before they become a problem, so your team can act before a late delivery impacts your customer.
  - list:
    - listitem:
      - img
      - heading "\"Being able to see a projected late delivery, you can't find that in other software. That is a big deal. It lets the dispatch team be proactive by identifying issues before they impact the customer experience.\"" [level=4]
      - paragraph: Marge Loveday, EVP, Logiscal
      - link "View Full Case Study":
        - /url: https://onfleet.com/blog/case-studies-logiscal/
        - text: View Full Case Study
        - img
  - heading "Keep Customers Informed Automatically, So Your Support Team Doesn't Have To" [level=2]
  - img "Live Tracking Page"
  - img "Automated Notifications"
  - img "Proof of Delivery"
  - heading "Live Tracking Page" [level=3]
  - paragraph: Give customers a live tracking page with real-time GPS, predictive ETAs, and driver chat, so they know when to expect their delivery, reducing missed handoffs and the support calls that follow.
  - heading "Automated Notifications" [level=3]
  - paragraph: Send branded SMS notifications at every stage of the delivery, so recipients always know where their order is and when it will arrive. Every message looks like it comes from you, even when the delivery is outsourced.
  - heading "Proof of Delivery" [level=3]
  - paragraph: Capture photos and signatures on every delivery, both in-house and external. Proof is centralized in Onfleet and shared instantly with customers to build trust and minimize disputes.
  - text: Unified Performance and Analytics
  - heading "Track Performance Across Every Driver and Delivery Partner, In One Place" [level=3]
  - heading "See Key Metrics By Driver" [level=4]
  - paragraph: Track on-time rate, service time, and average feedback rating for every driver in one place, so you always know who's performing and where to improve.
  - heading "Multi-Location Performance Tracking" [level=4]
  - paragraph: Give each team or location visibility into their own data while leadership gets a consolidated view across the entire operation, with no manual reporting needed.
  - heading "In-House vs. Third Party Analytics" [level=4]
  - paragraph: Compare your internal fleet and external courier partners against the same metrics, so you know exactly when outsourcing is working and when it isn't.

  - heading "Smart Dispatching" [level=3]

        - link "DashPass":

          - strong: DashPass
        - strong: "?"
      - paragraph: DashPass is DoorDash's membership program that unlocks exclusive savings at restaurants, grocery stores, and more. DashPass members get $0 delivery fees, reduced service fees, and special discounts on eligible orders at participating merchants.
      - paragraph:
        - text: DashPass is available in the U.S. and Canada, with some areas excluded. See full terms
        - link "here":
          - /url: /en-us/legal/article/cx-terms-and-conditions
        - text: .
      - heading "My DashPass Benefits did not apply to my last order?" [level=2]:
        - strong: My DashPass Benefits did not apply to my last order?
      - paragraph:
        - strong: "The most common reason:"
        - text: your order didn't meet the merchant's subtotal minimum.
      - paragraph: Your DashPass benefits only apply once your order meets a participating store's order minimum. If your order subtotal comes in under that amount, your DashPass savings won’t apply.
      - paragraph: To avoid this next time, look for the purple DashPass icon under the merchant's name — it means the store is eligible for DashPass, and the app will show you exactly how much more to add to reach the minimum.
      - 'img "Migrated from Salesforce: https://figment.file.force.com/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0Kd000000QuY3&feoid=00N2L00000AWqPe&refid=0EM2L000001UTRP"'

      - heading "I see an unauthorized charge of $9.99." [level=2]:
        - strong: I see an unauthorized charge of $9.99.
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: "Seeing an unfamiliar charge on your account can be alarming, and we’re here to help. A few things to check first:"
          - list:
            - listitem:
              - paragraph: Consider who else has access to your account. If a family member or partner has your login info, they may have placed an order using your saved payment information from a different device.
            - listitem:
              - paragraph: If you don't have a DoorDash account, consider anyone you've shared your credit card information with — they may have used it to place an order on their own account.
            - listitem:
              - paragraph: If your bank statement says "DoorDash DashPass" or "DashPass," that's a charge for your membership. You can verify it by opening Manage DashPass and checking Billing History.
      - heading "What else is included?" [level=2]:
        - strong: What else is included?
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: In addition to the DashPass savings above, members also enjoy exclusive benefits, like priority customer support and DashPass-only promotions.
      - heading "Will my DashPass benefits apply to both Caviar and DoorDash?" [level=2]:
        - strong: Will my DashPass benefits apply to both Caviar and DoorDash?
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Yes — as long as you use the same login information for both Caviar and DoorDash, your DashPass benefits will automatically be available on both platforms.
      - heading "Who is eligible for DashPass free trial?" [level=2]:
        - strong: Who is eligible for DashPass free trial?
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph:
            - text: We offer a free trial for users who have not previously tried DashPass (whether on a free or paid plan). Once your trial is over, you will be automatically enrolled in the membership plan you selected at sign-up and a payment method in your DoorDash account will be charged. Your membership will auto-renew on your membership billing date until you cancel. DoorDash may change the eligibility requirements for a free DashPass trial at any time without notice. See DashPass terms

            - text: .
      - heading "What will happen if I cancel my free trial?" [level=2]:
        - strong: What will happen if I cancel my free trial?
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: If you cancel during a trial period, your benefits will be terminated immediately. If you cancel after the billing date your subscription will be charged to your default payment method and DashPass benefits will be valid till the end of the billing cycle.

          - paragraph: DoorDash offers monthly and annual DashPass plans, plus discounted memberships for eligible users like students. See current DashPass plans for live pricing.

      - text: 13 min read
      - paragraph:
        - strong: Overview
      - paragraph: Your ratings help you understand your delivery quality on the platform and determine your eligibility for Rewards, incentives, and certain programs.
      - paragraph: Each rating measures a different part of your dashing experience — things like completing orders on time, delivering with high quality, and providing great customer service. We also work hard to ensure ratings are fair.

      - paragraph:
        - strong: How Rolling Ratings Work
      - paragraph: Some ratings are calculated on a “rolling basis.” This means that as you dash, ratings from past orders will be replaced by ratings from more recent orders.
      - paragraph: The graphic below helps illustrate how these rolling ratings work. This specific example uses acceptance rate, but other ratings are also calculated on a rolling basis (i.e., customer rating, completion rate, on-time rate, quality rate, and last 30-day orders).
      - 'img "Migrated from Salesforce: https://figment.file.force.com/dashers/servlet/rtaImage?eid=ka0fG0000000DLR&feoid=00N2L00000AWqPe&refid=0EMKd000007VZgb"'
      - paragraph: The acceptance rate is based on your 100 most recent offers. Each time you accept or decline a new offer, the oldest offer drops off, and your rate updates.
      - paragraph: This means that, if you decline an offer, it will take 100 more offers for this decline to drop off from your rating. This is why you do not always see an immediate change to your rating after accepting a number of new offers.
      - paragraph:
        - strong: See Your Last 100 Orders (In Select Areas)
      - paragraph: To make rolling ratings easier to understand, some Dashers can now see a detailed breakdown of their last 100 orders for acceptance rate and completion rate.
      - paragraph: "In this view, you can see:"
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: A full list of your last 100 orders, labeled as accepted, declined, completed, unassigned, or excluded
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Which orders were excused for reasons outside your control (such as store closures or system issues) and excluded from your rating calculation
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: How older orders roll off as new ones are added, and how that affects your rating over time
      - paragraph: "Note: This experience is only available in select areas. The detailed view is active when dashing in those areas, and you may see changes to your Acceptance Rate or Completion Rate if you dash in different locations."
      - paragraph:
        - strong: Customer Rating
      - paragraph: Your customer rating reflects how customers rate their delivery experience with you, not their food experience. It’s based on your last 100 customer ratings (out of 5 stars).
      - paragraph: If you receive a few low ratings, don’t worry. As you receive new customer ratings, older ones will drop off.
      - paragraph:
        - strong: "Fairness protections:"
      - paragraph: "To help make ratings more fair, we automatically remove any customer ratings you receive that are below 5 stars. Here are some examples:"
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Long wait times at restaurants
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: When the delivery or task is already expected to be very late when you accept it
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: When multiple Dashers before you unassign, causing the delivery to be late to the customer
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: When the delivery or task is late due to multiple orders being batched together for a single dash
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Extreme weather conditions
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Uniquely challenging dashing situations related to protests
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: System-wide outages
          - list:
            - listitem:
              - paragraph:
                - text: For other app issues, please see our troubleshooting guide
                - link "here":

      - paragraph:
        - strong: "Minimum customer rating required:"
        - text: "4.2"
      - paragraph:
        - strong: Customer rating FAQs
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Q:"
        - strong: Why didn’t my rating go up after a good delivery?
      - paragraph: "A: Customers don’t always leave ratings. If a customer doesn’t rate their order, it won’t affect your score."
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Q:"
        - strong: How can I improve my customer rating?
      - paragraph: "A: We can share a number of tips that could help you improve your rating, but do what works best for you. Here are a few tips that experienced Dashers use to maintain a high customer rating:"
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Ask the merchant to confirm all items are included without opening sealed bags.
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Use a hot bag to deliver food at the expected temperature.
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Separate hot and cold items during transport.
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Follow the merchant’s pickup instructions and the customer’s drop-off instructions.
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Keep the customer updated! Customers always appreciate a heads-up when you’re running a few minutes late or if any clarification is needed for the offer.
      - paragraph:
        - strong: Completion rate
      - paragraph: Your completion rate is the % of accepted offers you finish. It’s based on your last 100 accepted offers. You can increase your completion rate by making sure every offer you accept is delivered to the customer.
      - paragraph: Since it is a rolling rating, if the newest accepted offer is completed and the oldest is not, your average increases. If the newest accepted offer is not completed and the oldest accepted offer is, your average decreases.
      - paragraph: Once you have passed 100 lifetime orders, each additional order will only have a 1% max impact on your average.
      - paragraph:
        - strong: "Minimum completion rate required:"
        - text: 90%
      - paragraph:
        - text: In select areas, you can tap into
        - strong: Completion Rate
        - text: to see exactly which of your last 100 orders are affecting your score. Excluded orders are not included in your rating calculation.
      - paragraph:
        - strong: Completion rate FAQs
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Q:"
        - strong: Why isn’t my completion rate improving?
      - paragraph: "A: See “How Rolling Ratings Work” at the top of the page. Ratings update based on your last 100 accepted orders, so it may take several completed orders before you see an increase. The best way to improve your completion rate is to consistently complete your accepted orders."
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Q:"
        - strong: What if I need to unassign from an order?
      - paragraph: "A: We understand that you may sometimes be unable to complete an order that you accept. In cases when you attempt to complete the order, but are unable to do so for reasons outside of your control (e.g., in the case of an emergency), we will excuse the unassign. Otherwise, you will need to maintain a 90% completion rate in order to stay active."
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Q:"
        - strong: Will my ratings be affected if I unassign from an offer?
      - paragraph: "A: Yes, unassigning from an offer yourself or unassigning by support will affect your completion rate, unless it’s marked as “worry-free” in the app. You will receive a notification on your app when you accept an offer, but later unassign from it. It will also notify you that completion rates below 90% could result in account deactivation."
      - paragraph:
        - strong: Acceptance rate
      - paragraph: Your acceptance rate is how often you accept offers out of your last 100 received.There’s no minimum requirement, but a higher acceptance rate can help you stay busy and factor into your Rewards status. You can raise your acceptance rate by consistently accepting offers.
      - paragraph:
        - text: In select areas, tapping into
        - strong: Acceptance Rate
        - text: shows a detailed view of your last 100 offers and how each one impacts your rating. Excluded offers are not included in your rating calculation.
      - paragraph:
        - strong: Acceptance rate FAQs
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Q:"
        - strong: I am accepting deliveries, but why isn't my acceptance rate going up?
      - paragraph: "A: See “How Rolling Ratings Work” at the top of the page. It may take a large number of accepted offers in a row for you to see an improvement in your rating. The best way to push out declined offers from your score is to consistently accept offers."
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Q:"
        - strong: Will declining offers hurt my ability to dash?
      - paragraph: "A: You can always accept or decline offers based on your preferences, and there is no minimum acceptance rate requirement. However, Dashers who accept more offers will be more likely to qualify for higher rewards status."
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Q:"
        - strong: What happens if I let the timer run out?
      - paragraph: "A: If the timer runs out, it counts as a decline. You can tap Pause in your app anytime if you’re not ready for new offers."
      - paragraph:
        - strong: On-time rate
      - paragraph: The new on-time rate is an updated version of the on-time/early rating that is more responsive and transparent.
      - paragraph: Your on-time rate measures how often you complete offers within the expected delivery time shown when you accepted them, based on your last 100 completed offers. For batched orders, they’re treated as a single offer for on-time rate purposes. Offers that include shopping and successfully disputed offers will not count towards your on-time rate.
      - paragraph: We know that sometimes a delivery is late for reasons outside your control. If a prior delivery has been excused, you’ll see that reflected on the delivery details in your on-time rate
      - paragraph:
        - strong: On-time rate FAQs
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Q:"
        - strong: How do you determine the original delivery time shown on the offer screen?
      - paragraph: "A: The delivery time shown on the offer screen is calculated to ensure Dashers can deliver orders on time and safely. It factors in expected store wait time, driving distance, traffic, speed limits, and other data."
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Q:"
        - strong: When is a delivery considered late?
      - paragraph: "A: A delivery is counted as late if it’s completed after the expected delivery time shown when you accepted the offer. In order to maintain fairness and safe driving, we regularly review and recalibrate our expected delivery times based on several factors, including actual delivery times."
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Q:"
        - strong: Why does my “pick up by” or “deliver by” time sometimes change during a delivery?

      - paragraph:
        - text: "Q:"
        - strong: Will this rating impact my experience as a Dasher?
      - paragraph: "A: This rating aims to give Dashers like you clear insights into your last 100 deliveries. Your on-time rate may also affect your Rewards qualification and other aspects of the Dasher experience, depending on your location. Check your Dasher app for details."
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Q:"
        - strong: Are all delivery types included in the last 100 on-time rating?
      - paragraph: "A: No. Shop & Deliver and Parcel offers are not counted toward the on-time rate."
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Q:"
        - strong: Do I need to do anything to see this new experience?
      - paragraph: "A: No, you can see your new rating simply by tapping into Ratings in the bottom menu, then in your ‘on-time rate’. If you don’t see it, try updating to the most recent version of your Dasher app."
      - paragraph:
        - text: "Q:"
        - strong: How do I dispute deliveries?
      - paragraph: "A: You can dispute late deliveries directly within the app. If you are unable to dispute at any moment, completing additional deliveries will enable you to dispute successfully again."

        - strong: "Note:"

        - text: "Q:"

      - paragraph: "A: If you are late on pickup and drop off, and your pickup delay is excluded, your delivery may still be marked late due to a late drop-off."
      - paragraph:

        - text: on your pickup screen in the DoorDash app. This protection will remain active so long as you arrive on time, stay at the restaurant, pick up the order as soon as it’s ready, and leave right after pickup.

    - heading "Providing a more straightforward replacements experience" [level=1]

    - paragraph: We’re always seeking ways to improve your experience and to better support you to deliver shopping excellence. We’ve heard from shoppers that making carefully considered replacements that customers appreciate takes a lot of thought and effort, and it’s not always a simple choice. Today we’re announcing a new experience that helps simplify how you make replacements–with helpful guidance and less guesswork so you can more easily deliver excellence with confidence.
    - heading "Improved in-app experience" [level=4]
    - paragraph: The app will now help you walk through the steps to choose the best replacement or make a refund when an item is sold out.
    - iframe
    - heading "Improved recommendations you can count on" [level=4]
    - figure:
      - img "Shopping_Quality_Replacements_(1).png"
    - paragraph: When the customer’s original item is sold out, we’ll provide replacement recommendations or suggest a refund based on your customer’s preferences to help you confidently make your decision. When you follow the replacement recommendations, you can positively impact your shopping quality score. A recommended replacement or customer pre-approved replacement counts as a replaced item towards your shopping quality score. If a customer requests a refund, refunding the original item counts as a requested refund towards your score. You’ll also enjoy rating protection, which means any customer rating below 5 stars will be removed if the customer reports a recommended or pre-approved replacement.
    - paragraph
    - heading "Less guesswork when comparing replacement options" [level=4]
    - paragraph: Scan up to three available replacement options that you think your customer would like. We’ll suggest which one to choose, or if you should refund based on your customer’s preferences. Replacing with the recommended in-stock replacement option means you’ll enjoy rating protection and can positively impact your shopping quality score. We’ll send all scanned options to your customer so they know what else is available in case they’d prefer something else.
    - heading "Seamless Updates for Effortless Communication" [level=4]
    - figure:
      - img "Customer_Replacements.png"
    - paragraph: Say goodbye to juggling between chat, notifications, and responses. You can now focus on shopping and your customers always stay up-to-date without the additional effort of back-and-forth messaging. Customers are notified automatically about replacements, refunds, and the other available options you scanned so you don’t need to follow up in chat. With a simple tap, customers can easily approve the replacement or refund you made when their item was sold out or request a different replacement from the scanned options you sent. If a customer requests any changes, we’ll automatically update your shopping list. Of course, chat is still available for anything that may need a personal touch.
    - heading "More resources to support delivering excellence" [level=4]

  - text: DELIVERY DRIVER APP FOR BUSINESSES
  - heading "The Delivery Driver App Built for Fleets That Can't Afford Mistakes" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Step-by-step guidance at every stop helps drivers get it right, with proof of delivery capture and a full chain of custody tracking across regions.
  - link "Talk to a delivery expert":
    - /url: /contact-sales
    - text: Talk to a delivery expert
    - img
  - link "Start a free trial":
    - /url: /signup
    - text: Start a free trial
    - img
  - img "The Onfleet driver app showing a drop-off task and the complete drop-off screen"
  - 'heading "The #1 Rated Driver App in Last-Mile Delivery" [level=2]'
  - paragraph: Drivers rate Onfleet 4.8+ stars across 7,000+ App Store and Google Play reviews. For your operation, that means fewer complaints to dispatch, faster ramp-up for new hires, and one less reason for drivers to leave.
  - 'link "Top-Rated Driver App on the App Store: 4.7 stars from 4.7k reviews on Apple App Store (opens in a new tab)"':
    - /url: https://itunes.apple.com/us/app/onfleet-driver/id1084013403?mt=8
    - img "Apple App Store"
    - text: "4.7"
    - img "1 of 5 Star Rating"
    - img "2 of 5 Star Rating"
    - img "3 of 5 Star Rating"
    - img "4 of 5 Star Rating"
    - img "5 of 5 Star Rating"
    - text: 4.7k
    - paragraph: Top-Rated Driver App on the App Store
  - 'link "Top-Rated Driver App on Google Play: 4.6 stars from 4.2k reviews on Google Play (opens in a new tab)"':
    - /url: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.onfleet.driver.app&hl=en_US
    - img "Google Play"
    - text: "4.6"
    - img "1 of 5 Star Rating"
    - img "2 of 5 Star Rating"
    - img "3 of 5 Star Rating"
    - img "4 of 5 Star Rating"
    - img "5 of 5 Star Rating"
    - text: 4.2k
    - paragraph: Top-Rated Driver App on Google Play
  - heading "What is a Delivery Driver App?" [level=2]
  - paragraph: A delivery driver app is the mobile tool your drivers use to receive routes, navigate to each stop, capture proof of delivery, and communicate with dispatchers and customers. For shippers and couriers, it is also where your delivery standards get enforced. It turns each driver's shift into real-time location data, verified handoffs, and performance records your operations team can act on.
  - list:
    - listitem: Fleet-wide GPS tracking and live ETAs
    - listitem: Enforced proof of delivery and chain of custody
    - listitem: ID scanning for age-restricted deliveries
    - listitem: Secure in-app chat with dispatch and customers
    - listitem: Offline mode for dead zones and large facilities
  - heading "When Your Driver App Can't Keep Up, Compliance, Performance, And Driver Retention Are At Risk" [level=2]
  - paragraph: "Most driver apps cover the basics, like GPS tracking and proof of delivery. A growing fleet needs more: consistent onboarding for every new driver, compliance enforced at every stop, and real-time visibility into every driver on the road. When the app falls short, drivers skip steps, miss stops, and call dispatch for answers, while delivery data stays disconnected from your other systems. Each gap becomes a failed delivery, a compliance risk, or a driver who eventually quits."
  - paragraph: Onfleet keeps drivers productive from their first shift and gives your team one place to manage internal drivers and external delivery partners, with the visibility, control, and compliance enforcement to keep performance consistent.
  - text: Results with Onfleet 4.8/5
  - paragraph: Driver Feedback Rating
  - text: 30%
  - paragraph: Reduction In Missed Deliveries
  - text: 99%
  - paragraph: On-Time Delivery
  - text: 1B+
  - paragraph: Miles Driven On Onfleet
  - heading "What Your Drivers Get, and What Your Operation Gets Back" [level=2]
  - text: COMPLIANCE & VERIFICATION
  - heading "Compliance and Verification Built Into Every Delivery" [level=3]
  - paragraph: Enforce your delivery standards and regulatory requirements across every driver and every stop, without relying on manual processes.
  - heading "Full Chain of Custody and Proof of Delivery" [level=4]
  - paragraph: Capture timestamped photos, signatures, barcode scans, and PIN code verification at every stop, creating a verifiable record for disputes, audits, and compliance.
  - heading "Custom Driver Requirements" [level=4]
  - paragraph: Require drivers to complete specific steps before a task can be closed, such as compliance checklists, entering cash collected, or confirming an ID check. Your process is followed consistently and documented across the entire fleet.
  - heading "ID Scanning for Age-Restricted Deliveries" [level=4]
  - paragraph: Drivers scan the recipient's ID in the app to verify age before handing over alcohol, cannabis, tobacco, or other regulated products, limiting your risk.
  - img "Driver app screens showing package verification and barcode scanning"
  - text: DELIVERY ACCURACY
  - heading "Successful Deliveries, Every Time" [level=3]
  - paragraph: Get every order to the right place, on time, with customers informed from dispatch to doorstep.
  - heading "Real-Time GPS Tracking" [level=4]
  - paragraph: Live driver location powers accurate ETAs, while geofencing and barcode scanning confirm the right package reaches the right place. Customers know when to expect their delivery, and dispatchers can step in before delays become failed deliveries.
  - heading "Driver Geofencing" [level=4]
  - paragraph: Location boundaries around each stop confirm drivers are at the right address before completing a task, preventing misdeliveries and ensuring accurate arrival data.
  - heading "Secure In-App Communications" [level=4]
  - paragraph: Drivers can reach recipients and dispatchers directly in the app to resolve access issues, gate codes, or changes on the spot, turning would-be failed attempts into successful deliveries.
  - img "Driver app geofencing alert preventing a delivery completed outside the delivery area"
  - text: DRIVER EXPERIENCE & RETENTION
  - heading "A Driver Experience That Keeps Fleets Productive" [level=3]

    - heading "Start for free. Pay as you grow." [level=1]
    - paragraph: One plan with every feature. You pay for the orders you deliver, not per driver or vehicle, with volume discounts as you grow.

    - paragraph: No credit card required

    - list:

        - text: Up to 100

        - emphasis: per order

        - emphasis: per order

        - text: 50,000+

        - emphasis: custom

    - heading "Every feature, on every plan" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Free plan comes with all features except for SMS notifications.
    - list:
      - listitem:
        - heading "Smart route optimization" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Optimized routes in minutes, with time windows, capacities and driver shifts.
      - listitem:
        - heading "Driver mobile app" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Turn-by-turn routes, stop details and navigation in Google Maps or Waze.
      - listitem:
        - heading "Real-time GPS tracking" [level=3]
        - paragraph: See every driver on the map and the timeline as the day unfolds.
      - listitem:
        - heading "Customer notifications" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Automatic email updates with accurate ETAs, in your brand.
      - listitem:
        - heading "Delivery tracker" [level=3]
        - paragraph: A live tracking link so customers can watch their delivery approach.
      - listitem:
        - heading "Proof of delivery" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Photos, signatures, barcode scanning and notes, time-stamped and synced instantly.
      - listitem:
        - heading "Unlimited drivers" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Add every driver, full-time or part-time, at no extra cost.
      - listitem:
        - heading "Unlimited dispatchers" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Your whole team can plan and adjust routes together.
      - listitem:
        - heading "View-only support dashboard" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Customer support can answer “where’s my order?” without touching routes.
      - listitem:
        - heading "Customer profiles (CRM)" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Every customer’s details, delivery notes and history in one place.
      - listitem:
        - heading "Business insights" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Monitor your performance and find more efficiency opportunities.
      - listitem:
        - heading "Integrations" [level=3]
        - paragraph: Bring orders in from Shopify, Zapier, our API and webhooks, or AI agents via MCP.

    - heading "How Our Latest Pilot Aims to Make Our Rewards Program Even More Flexible" [level=1]
    - paragraph: We're piloting an Overall Dasher Rating to make our rewards program even more flexible and accessible.
    - text: Dec 16, 2024
    - img "Dx Blog (US/CA/AU/NZ) - Scheduling Tips for Caregivers"
    - article:
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Since launching our rewards program earlier this year, we heard clear feedback from Dashers that they wanted more flexible ways to access it.
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: That’s why this week, we’re starting to pilot our new Overall Dasher Rating that will give Dashers more accessibility when it comes to our rewards program, and more flexibility on ways to deliver high-quality service and maintain their rewards status over time.
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: This pilot is available in a limited number of markets, and we’re eager to get feedback from Dashers before scaling this more broadly.
      - paragraph:
        - text: Earlier this year,
        - link "we launched":
          - /url: https://about.doordash.com/en-us/news/making-the-dashing-experience-even-better
        - text: our new Dasher Rewards program based on feedback that we heard time and time again from the Dasher community. We consolidated existing programs to create a rewards program that was easier to understand, more transparent in the Dasher app, and was more inclusive – three all-new tiers, with different metrics required to gain access to each.
      - paragraph: Since launching, we’ve continued to listen to feedback from Dashers, who have told us that they want the rewards program to have more flexibility and optionality. Simply put, every Dasher is different – some are more interested in taking every offer that comes their way, while others may be more selective based on their personal criteria. No matter the individual circumstances, we believe that if you deliver exceptionally high quality for consumers and merchants, you should be rewarded.
      - paragraph: "That’s why today, in select markets, we’re piloting an all-new Overall Dasher Rating to qualify Dashers for our Rewards program. Here’s how it works: In this pilot, the Overall Dasher Rating uses a composite score that ranges from 0 to 100, and gives Dashers a point value based on four metrics that are each weighted differently:"
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Acceptance Rate (25 points)
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Completion Rate (35 points)
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: On-Time Rate (30 points)
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Customer Rating (10 points)
      - paragraph: "A Dasher’s total Overall Dasher Rating score will inform which Rewards tier they’re eligible for:"
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: "Silver: 60 - 64 points"
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: "Gold: 65 - 74 points"
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: "Platinum: 75 - 100 points"
      - paragraph: "This new rating makes our Rewards program more flexible and more accessible by empowering Dashers to earn Rewards tiers in different ways. Here’s an example of how two Dashers with different metrics can gain access to rewards:"
      - img "Screenshot 2024-12-17 at 11.33.25 AM"
      - paragraph: With an Overall Dasher Rating of 75, both of these Dashers will unlock Platinum level, but the ways that they earned these points are completely different.
      - paragraph:
        - text: You can learn more about the Overall Dasher Rating
        - link "here":
          - /url: https://help.doordash.com/dashers/s/article/Overall-Dasher-Rating?language=en_US
        - text: and more about our Rewards tiers
        - link "here":
          - /url: https://help.doordash.com/dashers/s/article/Dasher-Rewards-Program-Pilot?language=en_US
        - text: . This is currently a limited pilot in select markets, and we’re excited to engage directly with Dashers for their feedback before determining whether to scale more broadly.

        - listitem: How to set up recipient notifications
    - heading "How to set up recipient notifications" [level=1]
    - paragraph: Enable, customize and set delivery time windows for recipient notifications
    - text: A Written by Ana Lopatina
    - time: August 4, 2026
    - article:
      - heading "Recipient notification costs" [level=1]
      - paragraph: Recipient Notifications sent by email are free of charge.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: Recipient notifications sent via SMS are charged at a flat cost set by our messaging partner Twilio.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph:
        - text: To find out more about Twilio SMS pricing information
        - link "click here":
          - /url: https://www.twilio.com/en-us/sms/pricing/
        - text: and select your location from the drop-down menu to see costs for your country.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph:
        - text: To find out more about SMS billing and invoices >
        - link "Click here":
          - /url: https://help.getcircuit.com/en/articles/3850399-how-to-monitor-usage-manage-your-invoices-and-billing-information
      - separator
      - heading "How to enable recipient notifications" [level=1]
      - paragraph: Go to Controls > External parties > Tracking notifications to turn recipient notifications on.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: With this feature enabled, Spoke will automatically send recipient notifications by email or SMS directly to your delivery recipients if recipient contact information (email address or phone number) has been provided. If no details are provided, no recipient notifications can be sent.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: Recipient contact information can be imported when you create a route or manually added to a stop.
      - paragraph
      - separator
      - paragraph
      - heading "How do recipient notifications work?" [level=1]
      - paragraph: Recipient notifications provide delivery/pickup updates and contain a dynamic tracking link where further details about a specific stop can be found.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: This dynamic tracking link gives the recipient real-time and useful information about their delivery.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: You can choose how many recipient notifications you want to send and at what stages of the delivery process. You can also select whether to send recipient notifications by email or SMS.
      - paragraph
      - separator
      - paragraph
      - heading "1st recipient notification" [level=1]
      - paragraph: The first recipient notification is sent when your driver starts their route.
      - paragraph: It tells delivery recipients that their package is out for delivery and what time their stop is expected to happen.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: Every recipient notification contains a tracking link that recipients can click to view a webpage with dynamic tracking information.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph:
        - text: What tracking information is displayed depends on the
        - link "recipient tracking preferences":
          - /url: "#h_498f1d2cd1"
        - text: that have been selected.
      - paragraph
      - link:
        - /url: https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/eevcziuc/1802422417/ac5b708a4102ff07034a96c5a24f/1.png?expires=1793539800&signature=a42479e8ddeeed1a717afb65b332a9f435ffc7226c4cbfbc2ac739a9cd9a692b&req=dSgnFM18n4VeXvMW1HO4zcxQUyt5gnYiqEGM9jmK2TvNavMdRv2pWi2u1cWm%0AzKnt2gQvcf3djdzjN0A%3D%0A
      - paragraph
      - heading "2nd recipient notification" [level=1]
      - paragraph: The second recipient notification is sent when the recipient's stop is next in the queue.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: It tells delivery recipients that their order is arriving shortly and what time their stop is expected to happen.
      - paragraph
      - separator
      - paragraph
      - heading "3rd recipient notification" [level=1]
      - paragraph: The third recipient notification is sent when your driver marks the stop as successful or failed.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: It tells delivery recipients that their stop has been attempted and was successful or failed and the dynamic tracking link now shows any proof of delivery that was collected by the driver.
      - paragraph
      - link:
        - /url: https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/eevcziuc/1802427909/33d212aebc1b788df9403efbdaf1/3.png?expires=1793539800&signature=e7c5e5afda07c8ea76c319e0663754fbef9dc14141e576434b7a56e7ff3f56e5&req=dSgnFM18mohfUPMW1HO4zeSClNNLZaPiAevRlNLPjzOOV7bzpzOSC1%2FGeXHp%0ALUzke8vHSkdsMiND8I0%3D%0A
      - paragraph
      - link:
        - /url: https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/eevcziuc/1802428102/cdad853e065fcf8ec89905269c36/4.png?expires=1793539800&signature=fa01c94998744f9c360fe821c4318930c69b87f243c46e7c2fd5e9c4a12a9a44&req=dSgnFM18lYBfW%2FMW1HO4ze5ie7dFPk0FvRHw7yDLbdqMsr5%2F%2FZPBhvAnrcHn%0AdcqidtTkfxl56liKzFw%3D%0A
      - paragraph
      - heading "How to select which recipient notifications are sent" [level=1]
      - paragraph: Go to Controls > External parties > Tracking notifications > Messages
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: Use the tick boxes to select which delivery and/or pickup messages you wish to send via email and/or SMS.
      - paragraph
      - separator
      - paragraph
      - heading "How to customize your recipient notification messages" [level=1]
      - paragraph: You can customize what your recipient notifications say.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: In Controls > External parties > Tracking notifications, you will find a range of default message templates.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: If you want to customize the content of your message templates, click one to edit it. The message will then appear in a pop-up editing box. Here, you can edit the SMS and email message content, then click > Save changes.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: You can change the language, custom fields, and wording of your recipient notifications to whatever you like.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: "Highlighted in the pop-up editing box are custom fields:"
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Team name
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Customer name
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Driver name
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Tracking link
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Date
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Position in queue
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Earliest time
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Latest time
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Seller name
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Seller Order ID
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Products
      - paragraph: These custom fields are completed using the data you import into Spoke to create a route, and you can click on a custom field to add it to your message.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph:
        - text: You can find a glossary of custom fields
        - link "here.":
          - /url: https://help.getcircuit.com/en/articles/3582870-prepare-your-spreadsheet-for-import
      - paragraph
      - heading "How to customize your SMS recipient notification sender name" [level=1]
      - paragraph: If you would like your SMS recipient notifications to appear as if they have been sent by your company, you can customize the sender name.
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Go to Controls > Tracking and notifications
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Scroll down to > Advanced SMS options
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Check that you are on the right plan to unlock this feature
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Add your custom sender name
      - paragraph: Custom sender names will only display if the recipient’s country supports alphanumeric sender IDs. In all other cases, SMS messages will automatically default to Spoke’s phone numbers.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph:
        - text: You can check the list of
        - link "countries that support alphanumeric sender IDs here":
          - /url: https://help.twilio.com/articles/223133767-International-support-for-Alphanumeric-Sender-ID
        - text: .
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: As of 1 July 2026, custom sender names are no longer available within Spoke Dispatch for SMS sent to Australian recipients. This is due to Australian regulations that require sender IDs to be registered per brand, a process Spoke is not able to manage on your behalf. You can set up your own Twilio integration using Spoke webhooks.
      - paragraph:
        - link "[See our setup guide →]":
          - /url: https://cdn.sanity.io/files/mod8xlf1/production/8dc7585f8ed9cb5e3bcbf82a6f4be2b9ab01775b.pdf
      - paragraph
      - heading "How to add your company logo to recipient tracking links" [level=1]
      - paragraph: If you are on the right plan to unlock this feature, you can add your company logo to recipient tracking links and printed manifests for a branded look.
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Go to Settings > Team settings > Company logo
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Click > Upload image > Select your logo file
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Zoom in/out to adjust the logo to fit the viewfinder
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Click > Save image
      - paragraph:
        - text: Your logo will now appear on all
        - link "recipient tracking links":
          - /url: https://help.spoke.com/en/articles/6979656-how-to-provide-customer-service-contact-details
        - text: and printed manifests.
      - paragraph
      - separator
      - paragraph
      - heading "How to select what tracking information you share with recipients" [level=1]
      - paragraph: Control what type of tracking information you share with recipients when they click the dynamic tracking link which is included in recipient notifications.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: "Go to > Recipient tracking preferences and select one of these options:"
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: ETA - Your delivery recipients will be shown an ETA time window
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Stops in queue - Your delivery recipients will be shown an ETA time window
          - paragraph: and their position in the queue eg Your stop is 10th in a queue of 30
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Driver live tracking - Your delivery recipients will be shown an ETA time window and their position in the queue. When they become the next stop they will be able to see and track the driver's location
          - paragraph
      - link:
        - /url: https://downloads.intercomcdn.com/i/o/1139952427/6f71510a3348c6875b47b4fe/Customer+notifications_.gif?expires=1793539800&signature=8c0c3d1b9e97cf717cbed956b6e63c6603d518b1962966f7ce324728b0c1f9a0&req=dSEkH8B7n4VdXvMW1HO4zboSZxRayu2zl78l7j%2FttGjenT5Q89UL%2FciTZu72%0AUEkya1wXy055%2B0XU0eg%3D%0A
      - paragraph
      - separator
      - paragraph
      - heading "How to set delivery time windows for recipient notifications" [level=1]
      - paragraph: Delivery time windows are used to create an ETA time window, which is included in recipient notifications.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: You can create fixed or dynamic delivery ETA time windows depending on your preferences.
      - paragraph
      - heading "How to set a fixed delivery time window" [level=1]
      - paragraph: A fixed delivery time window will apply to all stops and will not change regardless of route progress.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: Go to Controls > External parties > Tracking notifications > Time window preferences.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: Select > Fixed time window. Enter a ‘start time’ and ‘end time’ for your delivery time window.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: "Example: A fixed delivery time window of 9 am - 5 pm can be helpful for businesses that wish to send ETAs to recipients which are accurate to the nearest working day."
      - paragraph
      - heading "How to set a dynamic delivery window" [level=1]
      - paragraph: A dynamic time window will apply to all stops and update in real-time depending on the progress of the route.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: Go to Controls > External parties > Tracking notifications > Time window preferences.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: Select > Dynamic time window. Enter a ‘minimum time’ and ‘maximum time’ for your delivery time window.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: "Example: A dynamic time window with a minimum value of 30 minutes and a maximum value of 2 hours for a stop with an ETA of noon. This dynamic time window will show recipients a minimum delivery time of 11.30 am-12.30 pm, potentially increasing to a maximum delivery time of 10 am - 2 pm, depending on route progress."
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: A dynamic time window can be helpful for businesses wishing to send real-time ETAs to recipients, which are accurate to the nearest minute.
      - paragraph
      - separator
      - paragraph
      - heading "How to turn recipient delivery notes on/off" [level=1]
      - paragraph: When recipients receive a delivery notification and click on the tracking link, they will see more delivery details and the option to add delivery instructions for their driver.
      - paragraph
      - paragraph: This can be useful when recipients add information about hard-to-find addresses, but recipients can also misuse it, so there is the option to turn this feature off.
      - paragraph
      - list:
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Go to > Controls > External parties > Tracking notifications
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Toggle Enable recipient delivery notes to off
        - listitem:
          - paragraph: Recipients will no longer be given the option to add delivery notes for their driver
          - paragraph
      - separator
      - paragraph
